questions.q: At a party or social gathering, you usually:
questions.a: Mingle with many people, including strangers.
questions.b: Stick to a few people you already know well.

questions.q: After a long, busy week, you recharge by:
questions.a: Going out with friends or doing something highly stimulating.
questions.b: Spending quiet time alone or in a very low-key environment.

questions.q: When solving a problem, you tend to:
questions.a: Talk it out with others to figure out what you think.
questions.b: Think it through quietly in your head before sharing your thoughts.

questions.q: In conversations, you are more likely to:
questions.a: Jump in quickly and speak as you formulate your ideas.
questions.b: Listen and wait until you have a fully formed thought before speaking.

questions.q: Your social circle is typically:
questions.a: Wide and diverse; you have many friends and acquaintances.
questions.b: Small and close-knit; you have a few very deep friendships.

questions.q: When learning something new, you prefer:
questions.a: A broad overview of many different topics.
questions.b: To dive deep into one specific subject and master it.

questions.q: If your phone rings unexpectedly, you usually:
questions.a: Answer it eagerly, happy for the interaction.
questions.b: Let it go to voicemail or text back later, unless it’s urgent.

questions.q: In a group project, you naturally gravitate toward:
questions.a: Being the spokesperson or taking a highly collaborative role.
questions.b: Doing the research or independent work behind the scenes.

questions.q: How do you handle your personal space?
questions.a: My door is usually open; I don't mind people dropping by.
questions.b: I need my private space and prefer people to ask before entering.

questions.q: When it comes to taking action:
questions.a: I am quick to act and figure out the details as I go.
questions.b: I prefer to observe and think carefully before making a move.

questions.q: People who know you well would describe you as:
questions.a: Highly approachable and easy to get to know.
questions.b: Reserved and somewhat difficult to truly get to know.

questions.q: In a work or school environment, you prefer:
questions.a: An open-plan office or lots of group collaboration.
questions.b: A quiet, private workspace where you can focus without interruption.

questions.q: When you are passionate about a topic:
questions.a: You naturally share your enthusiasm with whoever is around.
questions.b: You keep your enthusiasm mostly to yourself or share only with trusted friends.

questions.q: If you have to wait in a long line, you:
questions.a: Easily strike up a conversation with the person next to you.
questions.b: Put in headphones, read, or just wait quietly in your own thoughts.

questions.q: You feel most confident when:
questions.a: You are interacting with the outside world and taking part in activities.
questions.b: You are in your own inner world, reflecting on your ideas and feelings.

questions.q: When reading a book or watching a movie, you care most about:
questions.a: The realistic details, facts, and literal events.
questions.b: The underlying themes, metaphors, and symbolic meanings.

questions.q: If someone gives you instructions, you prefer them to be:
questions.a: Step-by-step, highly detailed, and concrete.
questions.b: A general overview of the goal, leaving you to figure out the steps.

questions.q: You tend to trust:
questions.a: Past experience and proven methods.
questions.b: Gut instincts and future possibilities.

questions.q: In your daily life, you are more focused on:
questions.a: What is real, practical, and happening right now.
questions.b: What could be, imagining future scenarios and "what ifs."

questions.q: When describing an event that happened to you, you usually:
questions.a: Give a chronological, precise account of exactly what happened.
questions.b: Jump around, focusing on the impressions, feelings, or the "big picture" of the event.

questions.q: You are more naturally drawn to people who are:
questions.a: Grounded, realistic, and down-to-earth.
questions.b: Imaginative, theoretical, and unconventional.

questions.q: When facing a challenge at work or school, you prefer to:
questions.a: Use a standard, tried-and-true approach that you know works.
questions.b: Brainstorm a brand new, innovative way to solve the problem.

questions.q: Your learning style leans toward:
questions.a: Hands-on experience and practical application.
questions.b: Abstract concepts and theoretical discussions.

questions.q: You are more likely to notice:
questions.a: Small changes in your physical environment or a person's appearance.
questions.b: Shifts in mood, overarching patterns, or hidden meanings in a conversation.

questions.q: Which statement appeals to you more?
questions.a: "Keep your feet on the ground and focus on the facts."
questions.b: "Keep your head in the clouds and dream big."

questions.q: When planning a vacation, you prefer:
questions.a: A detailed itinerary with specific places, times, and practical logistics.
questions.b: A loose idea of where you are going, leaving plenty of room for spontaneous exploration.

questions.q: You are most bothered by:
questions.a: People who are overly theoretical and lack common sense.
questions.b: People who are too rigid and lack imagination.

questions.q: When you buy a new gadget, you usually:
questions.a: Read the manual carefully before turning it on.
questions.b: Turn it on immediately and start pressing buttons to see what it does.

questions.q: In a conversation, you prefer talking about:
questions.a: Actual events, specific details, and real-life experiences.
questions.b: Ideas, philosophies, and hypothetical situations.

questions.q: You believe the best way to improve a system is to:
questions.a: Tweak and refine the existing, practical elements.
questions.b: Tear it down and invent a completely new conceptual framework.

questions.q: When making an important decision, you rely more on:
questions.a: Objective logic, pros and cons, and cause-and-effect.
questions.b: Personal values, empathy, and how the decision affects people.

questions.q: If a friend comes to you with a problem, your first instinct is to:
questions.a: Offer practical solutions and help them fix the issue.
questions.b: Offer emotional support, validation, and a listening ear.

questions.q: You prefer to be praised for:
questions.a: Your competence, fairness, and intelligence.
questions.b: Your compassion, warmth, and helpfulness.

questions.q: When negotiating or arguing a point:
questions.a: You focus on the facts and strive to be objectively correct.
questions.b: You focus on maintaining harmony and ensuring everyone feels respected.

questions.q: Which is a worse flaw in a leader?
questions.a: Being overly emotional and letting personal feelings cloud their judgment.
questions.b: Being cold, rigid, and ignoring the human element of their decisions.

questions.q: When you have to deliver bad news, you:
questions.a: Get straight to the point and state the facts clearly.
questions.b: Soften the blow, carefully choosing your words to minimize hurt feelings.

questions.q: You are more naturally convinced by:
questions.a: A well-researched, logically sound argument.
questions.b: A passionate, emotionally resonant appeal.

questions.q: In a team setting, you are the person who:
questions.a: Points out the flaws in the plan to ensure it will actually work.
questions.b: Ensures everyone is getting along and feels included in the process.

questions.q: When someone makes a mistake, you are more likely to:
questions.a: Critique the error so they can learn and not repeat it.
questions.b: Encourage them and focus on what they did right to protect their confidence.

questions.q: You value justice and fairness, meaning:
questions.a: Everyone should be treated equally according to the rules, regardless of circumstances.
questions.b: Everyone should be treated with mercy and understanding based on their individual circumstances.

questions.q: If you have to fire or let go of an employee/team member:
questions.a: You focus on the business metrics and performance data that justify the decision.
questions.b: You agonize over the personal impact it will have on them and their family.

questions.q: Which statement sounds more like you?
questions.a: "The truth is more important than making people feel good."
questions.b: "Tact and harmony are more important than being brutally honest."

questions.q: When watching a movie, you get frustrated when:
questions.a: The plot has glaring logical holes or the characters act irrationally.
questions.b: The characters are unkind to one another or lack emotional depth.

questions.q: In your friendships, you prioritize:
questions.a: Mutual respect, intellectual stimulation, and reliability.
questions.b: Emotional intimacy, warmth, and unconditional support.

questions.q: You naturally ask yourself:
questions.a: "Does this make logical sense?"
questions.b: "Is this the right thing to do for the people involved?"

questions.q: When it comes to your daily schedule, you prefer to:
questions.a: Have a clear plan and stick to it.
questions.b: Keep your options open and go with the flow.

questions.q: How do you handle deadlines?
questions.a: I finish my work well ahead of time to avoid last-minute stress.
questions.b: I work in bursts of energy, often doing my best work right before the deadline.

questions.q: Your workspace (desk, room, or home) is usually:
questions.a: Organized, tidy, and everything has its proper place.
questions.b: A bit messy, but I know where everything is (organized chaos).

questions.q: When going on a trip, you prefer to:
questions.a: Pack days in advance and have a detailed itinerary.
questions.b: Pack the night before (or the morning of) and decide what to do when you get there.

questions.q: You feel the most satisfied when:
questions.a: A project is finished, checked off the list, and completely resolved.
questions.b: You are in the process of starting a new project and exploring new ideas.

questions.q: If plans suddenly change at the last minute:
questions.a: You feel stressed or annoyed because your schedule is disrupted.
questions.b: You adapt easily and often enjoy the spontaneous change of plans.

questions.q: How do you approach rules and guidelines?
questions.a: They are there for a reason and should be followed strictly.
questions.b: They are more like suggestions; they can be bent if the situation calls for it.

questions.q: When making a purchase (like a car or a computer):
questions.a: You research thoroughly, compare options, and make a firm decision quickly.
questions.b: You browse for a long time, keeping your options open in case something better comes along.

questions.q: Your to-do list usually:
questions.a: Dictates your day; you feel great when you cross items off.
questions.b: Is more of a vague mental guide; you do whatever feels most pressing at the moment.

questions.q: You are more likely to:
questions.a: Work first, play later.
questions.b: Mix work and play, or play first and work later.

questions.q: When someone asks, "What are you doing this weekend?", you say:
questions.a: Exactly what you have planned, down to the times and locations.
questions.b: "I'm not sure yet, I'll just see how I feel when the weekend gets here."

questions.q: In your personal life, you seek:
questions.a: Closure and resolution; you dislike leaving things hanging.
questions.b: Open-endedness; you like keeping your options open.

questions.q: When you are supposed to meet someone at 2:00 PM:
questions.a: You arrive at 1:50 PM to be safe.
questions.b: You arrive at 2:02 PM, or text them that you are "almost there" at 2:05 PM.

questions.q: You prefer environments that are:
questions.a: Structured, predictable, and highly organized.
questions.b: Flexible, dynamic, and adaptable.

questions.q: Which phrase describes you best?
questions.a: "A place for everything, and everything in its place."
questions.b: "Let’s cross that bridge when we come to it."
